record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one rigorously prove universality for other random-data numerical algorithms discussed in the paper, such as the conjugate-gradient method for solving Ax=b with random A and random b?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting and challenging open problem to prove universality rigorously for any of the other numerical algorithms discussed in [40]. The conjugate gradient algorithm, in particular, to compute the solution of the linear system Ax = b with A and b random, seems to be ‘within reach’.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $N\times N$ random positive-definite (e.g. sample covariance or Wigner-type) matrix drawn from an ensemble whose entries are independent up to symmetry and satisfy standard moment conditions, and let $b\in\mathbb{R}^N$ be an independent random vector (e.g. with i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$). Apply the conjugate-gradient algorithm to solve the linear system $Ax=b$: starting from $x_0=0$, $r_0=b$, $p_0=r_0$, iterate
$$\alpha_k=\frac{\langle r_k,r_k\rangle}{\langle p_k,Ap_k\rangle},\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k p_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_k Ap_k,\quad \beta_k=\frac{\langle r_{k+1},r_{k+1}\rangle}{\langle r_k,r_k\rangle},\quad p_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_k p_k.$$
For a prescribed tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, let $T_{N,\varepsilon}(A,b)$ denote the halting time, i.e. the smallest $k$ with $\|r_k\|/\|r_0\|<\varepsilon$. Rigorously prove a universality theorem for the conjugate-gradient algorithm: show that, after appropriate centering and scaling, the fluctuations of $T_{N,\varepsilon}$ (and of related statistics such as residual norms at iteration $k$) converge as $N\to\infty$ to a limiting distribution which depends only on a few parameters of the ensemble and not on the fine details of the laws of the entries of $A$ and $b$.
artifact.category_tag: Universality for numerical algorithms on random matrices
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Deift and Trogdon showed that the conjugate-gradient algorithm on well-conditioned Wishart matrices is almost deterministic, and Paquette–Trogdon (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2023) established a central limit theorem / universality for the residual norms produced by the conjugate-gradient and MINRES algorithms on sample covariance matrices satisfying standard moment conditions. Universality results have also been obtained for other related algorithms (Toda, eigenvalue algorithms). However, full universality (e.g. for general ensembles and the halting time itself in all natural regimes) is not yet established in complete generality, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Universality for the Conjugate Gradient and MINRES Algorithms on Sample Covariance Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Paquette and Trogdon proved a central limit theorem for norms of residual vectors produced by the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms applied to a wide class of sample covariance matrices satisfying standard moment conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Universality (CLT) for residual norms of CG and MINRES on sample covariance matrices has been proved.

status_evidence.title: The conjugate gradient algorithm on well-conditioned Wishart matrices is almost deterministic
status_evidence.snippet: Deift and Trogdon proved that the number of iterations required to solve a random positive definite linear system with the conjugate gradient algorithm is almost deterministic for large matrices, via a four-moment theorem for the spectral measure.
status_evidence.claim: Almost-deterministic / universality-type behavior of CG halting time has been rigorously established on well-conditioned Wishart matrices.

status_evidence.title: Smoothed Analysis for the Conjugate Gradient Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Menon and Trogdon contributed work on smoothed analysis for the conjugate gradient algorithm in a special issue on universality in random matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress via smoothed analysis exists.
